title: Executive Circumvention of Congressionally Assigned Smithsonian Governance
proposed_area: A-17 — Independent Agencies and Regulatory Neutrality (provisional)
institutional_defect: A President may use executive-controlled property, appropriations administration, contracts, or other agency leverage to displace or circumvent governance authority that Congress assigned to a cross-branch public trust institution, without obtaining a statutory change or a decision through that institution's governing board.
distinctness_rationale: The asserted accuracy of a museum exhibit is the administration's justification, but the potentially distinct institutional weakness is allocation of control. FACT-001 and the former FACT-007 framing concern information integrity; REG-001 concerns agency independence and functional nullification but presently focuses on executive-branch entities and disablement; JUD-011 concerns executive nullification of enacted mandates; FUND-001, RET-001, and HER-001 own fiscal implementation, coercive leverage, and physical civic-property mechanisms only when those mechanisms are actually implicated. The Smithsonian's branch-independent trust structure and attempted circumvention without demonstrated disablement may therefore expose an unowned boundary problem.
existing_coverage_considered: FACT-001; former FACT-007 issue #174; REG-001; JUD-011; FUND-001; RET-001; HER-001; EO 14253 and its existing HER-001/FUND-001 source routes
counterargument: The order may remain noncoercive executive speech implemented lawfully on NPS-controlled property; executive agencies may possess valid property, appropriations, procurement, or contract authority; the Board of Regents remains legally free to reject the administration's position; Congress knowingly created a mixed governance and funding arrangement; and ordinary judicial review may already supply an adequate remedy without a new institutional rule.
unresolved_questions: Identify title and jurisdiction over the affected walkways and land; the NPS authority and appropriation for signs or temporary exhibits; any OMB, GSA, Interior, funding, procurement, or contract action directed at the Smithsonian; the Board and Secretary's response; whether implementation produces reviewable injury; standing, sovereign-immunity, cause-of-action, and remedy questions; whether a court treats the action as lawful executive speech, lawful property management, coercion, or ultra vires circumvention; whether existing remedies are adequate; and whether the best eventual route is an expansion of REG-001 or JUD-011, a distinct proposal, or mechanism-specific placement in FUND-001, RET-001, or HER-001.
recommendation: Retain as a preliminary candidate and monitor implementation and litigation without presuming unlawfulness. Reassess when signs or exhibits are installed, an implementing funding, contract, procurement, or property directive is released, the Board or Congress takes material action, or a complaint, injunction, appellate decision, or merits ruling addresses the authority question. If verified conduct materially circumvents the Board's statutory governance, test expansion of REG-001/JUD-011 against a distinct cross-branch-institution remedy; otherwise route the episode to the mechanism-specific existing owner or close it as adequately governed by existing law.
